name: Evolution & Change
one_liner: Welcome scope evolution; change requests become work items, absorbed by releases and iterations.
purpose: The Evolution and Change dimension highlights the need to recognise and welcome the natural evolution of project scope, because both provider and requestor gain a better understanding of the problem as the project progresses. Changes that seriously impact the development aspect are still managed within the overall project change management process, and change requests must be translated into Work Items that populate the Work Items List. PM²-Agile then addresses that evolution through Release Planning and through Iterative and Incremental Development.

fields.what: The theme highlights the need to recognise and welcome the natural evolution of the project scope as understanding grows.
fields.pollux: Each quarter the reporting requirements change; POLLUX expects that.

fields.what: Changes seriously impacting the development aspect should be managed within the overall project change management process.
fields.pollux: PM²-Agile does not delete PM² governance, gates or change control.

fields.what: Agile Team Members should participate in change requests to ensure proper understanding of what is being asked.
fields.pollux: Lamarr and Babbage sit in when a new reporting demand arrives.

fields.what: Change requests must be translated into the corresponding Work Items that populate the Work Items List.
fields.pollux: A new national-authority requirement enters Curie's list, not a side channel.

fields.what: Those work items are prioritised and later implemented in the scope of one or more iterations.
fields.pollux: Absorbed into a two-week iteration rather than a change board queue.

fields.what: Focuses on the high-level macro planning of the complete known project scope, describing what each release contains and when.
fields.pollux: Four releases from 29 Mar 2029 to 20 Dec 2029.

fields.what: It creates a project coarse-grained plan used to guide the development of fine-grained plans for each iteration.
fields.pollux: The release plan sets what each fortnight's iteration plan must serve.

fields.what: A properly estimated and prioritised Work Items List is critical to ensure proper release planning.
fields.pollux: Without Curie's prioritised list the four release dates mean nothing.

fields.what: Release Planning is continuous and should reflect the team's growing knowledge, improving planning accuracy with updated Release Plans.
fields.pollux: Release Planning happens at least once per iteration on POLLUX.

fields.what: With Release Planning the A-PCT can better adjust itself in response to the need for increasing manpower.
fields.pollux: Justifies the two seconded Levallois Systems members.

fields.what: Release Planning makes it visible to the Product Owner how the solution evolves, giving time to react if things go off plan.
fields.pollux: Curie sees Release 3 slipping before the 27 Sep 2029 date arrives.

fields.what: The main output of Release Planning; part of the Development Work Plan and key to communicating progress and trends to senior management.
fields.pollux: What you show Medici instead of a Gantt chart.

fields.what: A system built in a series of increments, each adding a subset of the final functionality, growing more complete across iterations.
fields.pollux: Read-only views first, then reconciliation, then scenarios, then self-service.

fields.what: PM²-Agile relies on incremental development to facilitate planning, breaking the solution up and organising it by a specific strategy.
fields.pollux: The four-release split is that strategy made explicit.

fields.what: Time must be set aside to review and improve parts of the system based on stakeholder feedback and the team's self-learning.
fields.pollux: Review and retrospective on the last day of every iteration.

fields.what: In PM²-Agile all iterations are timeboxed and of the same duration, which sets the heartbeat and reduces uncertainty.
fields.pollux: Two weeks, every time, for eighteen months.

fields.what: Regular iterations keep the team from going off limits; small ones make feedback-driven changes easier to apply.
fields.pollux: A new report view now costs one iteration instead of one quarter (SC2).

fields.what: Small regular iterations let teams postpone design decisions to the last responsible moment, narrowing options as they learn.
fields.pollux: Einstein defers the scenario engine choice until Release 3 is planned.

traps: Incremental and iterative differ: increments add functionality, iterations refine it.
All PM²-Agile iterations are timeboxed and of the same duration.
Change requests do not bypass PM² change management — they also become work items.
The Release Plan is part of the Development Work Plan, not a separate schedule.
Set Based Design defers decisions to the last responsible moment, not indefinitely.
